name: Question 1
problem:
Given that $x=3$ and $x=-2$ are solutions to the equation ${x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+7x-30=0,$ find the remaining solutions in the form $a\pm b\,\text{i},$ where $b$ is **non-negative** number.

$x=$

$\pm $
{{field-2}}$\text{i}$
worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+7x-30.$ Since ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=-2$ are roots of $f(x),$ then according to the factor theorem, 

$$
(x-3)(x+2)={x}^{2}-x-6
$$

is a factor of $f(x).$

Next, we find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by ${x}^{2}-x-6$ using polynomial division.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,{x}^{2}-2x+5 \\ {x}^{2}-x-6 & \,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+7x-30\,\,} \\  & \,{{x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,-2{x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}+7x-30 \\  & \,{\,-\,2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+12x}_{―} \\  & \,5{x}^{2}-5x-30 \\  & \,{5{x}^{2}-5x-30}_{―} \\  & \,0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $f(x)=({x}^{2}-x-6)({x}^{2}-2x+5).$

To find the remaining two roots, we solve ${x}^{2}-2x+5=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x+5 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-2x+1)+5-1 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-4 \\ x-1 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ x & =1\pm 2\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the remaining solutions to our original equation, apart from $x=3$ and $x=-2,$ are $x=1\pm 2\,\text{i}.$
